mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05), or the effect is reversed in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) of at least 2% above the prior quarter coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% from previous quarter
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS change and SPX 20d returns (R² < 0.01) or returns are negative during the identified labor expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 101.5 (2017=100 index) for two consecutive months, it signals resilient supply-side momentum that boosts investor confidence and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive SPX 60d returns during the identified INDPRO expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 260) over a month suggests the Fed is less likely to raise rates, lowering discount rates and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 260 for one month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative or flat during the CPIAUCSL decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below 230K indicate labor market softening, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and reducing discount rates, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the identified softening (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both the S&P 500 futures (not in proxies, but as context) and a combination of falling unemployment (PAYEMS) and rising industrial production (INDPRO) occur simultaneously over a month, the dual positive demand signals reinforce equity optimism and drive positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and INDPRO increases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant interaction effect (IC < 0.05) or returns are not statistically different from baseline during the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (not directly observable here; instead, use HOUST as a proxy for housing market strength, which often correlates with labor market expansion) above 1500 units for three consecutive months predicts stronger consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60d SPX returns during the identified HOUST expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months), the higher real interest environment suppresses equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the tightening (p > 0.05) or the effect reverses in out-of-sample tests.
